source.author: verg
source.text: qualis ubi abruptis fugit praesaepia vinclis tandem liber equus campoque potitus aperto aut ille in pastus armentaque tendit equarum aut assuetus aquae perfundi flumine noto emicat arrectisque fremit cervicibus alte luxurians, luduntque iubae per colla, per armos.
source.text_original: qualis ubi abruptis fugit praesaepia vinclis / tandem liber equus campoque potitus aperto / aut ille in pastus armentaque tendit equarum / aut assuetus aquae perfundi flumine noto / emicat arrectisque fremit cervicibus alte / luxurians, luduntque iubae per colla, per armos.
source.text_english: As when a horse, his stall bonds burst, has at last fled free and gained the open field, either he makes for pasture and the mares’ herds, or, accustomed to be drenched in water by the well-known stream, he springs out and neighs high, luxuriating with lifted neck, and his mane plays over neck and shoulders.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_original: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis / fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras / ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus / rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_english: First we sing of the sea passages made traversable by the great sons of the gods, and of the prophetic ship, which, daring to follow the Scythian shores of Phasis and, driven on, to break through its course amid the middle mountain ridges, at last settled on fiery Olympus.
